page: Amazon Web Services c4.large is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core of an Intel Xeon E5-2666 v3 processor running at 2.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 1.88 GB of RAM per core. It operates under the Xen hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is limited to a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate moderate single-core capabilities but overall constrained multi-core and memory throughput. The single-core stress-ng CPU test and single-threaded gzip compression achieve average tier results. However, multi-core performance is limited, with the stress-ng multi-core test and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth is also restricted, with uncached read and write speeds measuring 13.03 GB/sec and 11.47 GB/sec respectively.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4.large represents an entry-level dedicated compute option. It avoids the CPU credit limitations of burstable instances but offers lower resource density compared to newer generation hardware. Given the 4.0 GB memory limit and lack of local storage, this instance is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded compute tasks, basic web serving, or small-scale utility workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation but do not demand high memory bandwidth or intensive multi-core processing.
